name: TerraFirma
what: Robotic construction: retrofits and remotely/autonomously operates heavy excavation machinery with its own planning and orchestration software; operates the fleet itself.
Autonomous steel-fabrication factory in Cincinnati run on its own 'Factory OS'; sells fabricated steel.

name: Machina Labs
what: Software-defined factories that form, weld, assemble and finish complex metal structures with AI-guided robots, no dedicated tooling; aerospace and defense customers.

name: Re:Build Manufacturing
what: PE-style roll-up of US manufacturers with a shared tech layer. Comp for 'buy plants + add software' vs greenfield.

name: SendCutSend
what: Instant-quote online sheet-metal and CNC service that owns and runs its own factories (laser, waterjet, bending, machining, finishing); bootstrapped-style growth to a $1B valuation.

name: Senra Systems
what: Designs and manufactures aerospace wire harnesses in its own plant on proprietary software (digital-twin conversion, automated work instructions, live status) plus automation.

name: Arda
what: AI that learns from factory video and coordinates machines and workers in plants owned by others; co-founded by ex-OpenAI chief research officer Bob McGrew.

name: Mind Robotics
what: Industrial robots that learn tool use and variable factory tasks from video of skilled operators; automotive manufacturing first (VW, Rivian on cap table).

name: CuspAI
what: Generative AI for materials discovery (search engine over possible materials), with lab validation partners; first use cases in carbon capture and energy materials.

name: Periodic Labs
what: AI 'scientist' plus autonomous labs: models propose materials, robots synthesize and test them, results train the next round; first targets include superconductors and heat-dissipation materials for chips.

name: Radical AI
what: AI plus self-driving labs for materials design (alloys, coatings) for defense, aerospace and energy; AlleyCorp-incubated, Gerbrand Ceder (Berkeley) co-founder.

name: Mariana Minerals
what: Vertically integrated, software-driven critical-minerals producer (lithium, copper, nickel, cobalt, rare earths) for energy, AI and defense supply chains.

name: Nox Metals
what: YC S25 company building automated metals factories: software-driven cut-to-size metal supply, quoting in minutes instead of days.

name: Nucor
what: Largest US steelmaker; electric-arc minimills; benchmark for metals margins and reshoring narrative.

name: Reliance (Reliance Steel & Aluminum)
what: Largest North American metals service center. Benchmark for service-center economics and M&A.

name: Ryerson
what: Public metals service center (cut-to-size, processing). The incumbent Nox Metals is rebuilding.

name: Divergent Technologies
what: Divergent Adaptive Production System (DAPS): AI-designed, additively printed and robotically assembled metal structures for automotive, aerospace and defense; owns the factory and licenses the system.

name: Freeform
what: Factory-as-a-service for metal additive parts: in-house printers, sensors, controls and ML monitor and adjust metal formation in real time; prototypes to production without the customer building AM infrastructure.

name: Hadrian
what: Autonomous precision-parts factories for aerospace and defense (machining, now casting/forging/additive); AI platform reads legacy drawings and automates manufacturing and inspection; also offers factories-as-a-service.

name: Isembard
what: Network of software-defined precision machining facilities in the UK/Europe for aerospace, defense and energy; rebuilding sovereign precision-parts capacity.

name: Precision Castparts (Berkshire)
what: Incumbent in aerospace castings/forgings; the capacity startups are selling against.

name: Proto Labs
what: Public digital manufacturer that owns its plants (injection molding, CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing). Closest public owner-operator comp for GM/capex.

name: Xometry
what: Public marketplace for custom parts; no plants (asset-light). The anti-thesis comp: software without owning production.
